source_documents.title: A zero intrinsic fluorescence Cy5 probe with dual-PET quenching for highly sensitive and instrument-independent HClO imaging in tumor and wound models

reference_evidence_units.quote: By integrating an electrondeficient quinolinium at the Cy5 meso-position (primary PET channel) with a dimethylthiocarbamate recogni tion unit (secondary PET quencher)
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Two quenchers: the meso-quinolinium and the dimethylthiocarbamate.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The dual-PET mechanism was validated by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which corroborated efficient electron transfer from the Cy5 core to both quenching units (Fig. 1b).
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Orbital energies place both quenchers for electron transfer with the Cy5 core.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Experimentally, this concerted quenching yielded an undetectable ab solute fluorescence quantum yield (ΦF) for Cy5Ql-HClO
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Phi_F of the probe is below detection; Cy5Ql (released dye) 8.69%, Cy5 14.9%.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The quinolinium at the meso-position provides the first PET channel (LUMO lies within Cy5 band gap). The second channel involves the dimethylthiocarbamate group. Although its HOMO is not between Cy5 HOMO and LUMO, ΔE = EHOMO, fluorophore – EHOMO, quencher = 0.12 eV < < 0.6 eV threshold [32].
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO, Cy5Ql-H2O2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Quinolinium LUMO inside the Cy5 gap (d-PET); thiocarbamate HOMO 0.12 eV below the Cy5 HOMO (a-PET).

reference_evidence_units.quote: This analog retains only the primary quinoliniumbased PET quencher, the phenylborate recognition group displays none PET effect (Fig. 1c, and Fig. S13). As anticipated, it exhibited measurably higher background fluorescence and a significantly greater absolute quantum yield compared to Cy5Ql-HClO (Fig. 1d), and lower SBR
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-H2O2 vs Cy5Ql-HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: With only the quinolinium quencher the probe keeps Phi_F 0.73%.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the intact probe, the electron-deficient quinolinium efficiently suppresses Cy5 fluorescence. HClO-specific cleavage of the dimethylthiocarbamate triggers a self-elimination reaction via a p-hydroxybenzyl alcohol linker, releasing neutral quinoline
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO + HClO
reference_evidence_units.statement: The reaction releases the neutral-quinoline dye Cy5Ql, removing both quenchers.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Fluorescence lifetime measurements revealed comparable decay kinetics for Cy5Ql-HClO and the parent dye Cy5Ql, with both exhibiting lifetimes in the range of 3–5 ns.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO vs Cy5Ql
reference_evidence_units.statement: Probe and released dye have similar 3-5 ns lifetimes.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: An undetectable quantum yield with an unchanged lifetime suggests the measured decay comes from a residual emitting fraction; the paper does not discuss this.

reference_evidence_units.quote: DLS confirms no aggregation at con centrations up to 1 mM (Fig. 2h)
reference_evidence_units.subject: Cy5Ql-HClO

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PET to the meso-quinolinium alone lowers the emission (Phi_F 0.73% vs 8.69% for the released dye); the boronate adds no PET channel.

contrast_group.varied_factor: recognition group on the N-benzyl of the meso-quinolinium Cy5 (dimethylthiocarbamate vs pinacol boronate)
contrast_group.paper_difference: With the thiocarbamate (second PET quencher) the probe is dark (Phi_F undetectable); with the boronate (no PET) background emission remains (Phi_F 0.73%).
